oracle_scope_policy: post-settlement checks may assert only the visible requirement and parent-visible public contracts

requirements.visible_requirement: Restrict the TypeScript limitFunction input type to asynchronous functions while preserving its existing argument and promised-result inference.
Reject invalid concurrency at limiter construction with the documented validation error before any task is scheduled, without producing a secondary callback error.
Treat an omitted or undefined concurrency argument as invalid instead of silently constructing a limiter.
Accept positive Infinity as concurrency and run without a concurrency cap while preserving rejection of other invalid values.
Allow the exported pMapSkip sentinel as a TypeScript Mapper return value without weakening the mapper input or ordinary result types.
Require finite concurrency values to be positive integers and reject fractional values using the existing argument-validation error contract.
Validate the input as an iterable and the mapper as a function before mapping, and reject invalid concurrency values according to the parent-visible API contract.
Drain every queued entry in order, including entries whose value is undefined, and leave the queue empty.
Add a peek method that returns the current front value without dequeuing it and returns undefined for an empty queue, with matching runtime and TypeScript surfaces.
Make TypeScript accept callCount only for functions returned by onetime while preserving the wrapped function's call signature.
Expose callCount as a property of the TypeScript default export rather than as a named export, preserving its wrapped-function input and numeric return types.
When the throw option is enabled, every invocation after the first must throw the intended onetime error rather than failing through an undefined stored function.
The public map method must work when called after being detached from the limiter object, with the same concurrency and result-order behavior as a direct method call.
Pass each source element's zero-based source index as the mapper's second argument in both runtime and TypeScript declarations while preserving result order.
Forward all arguments supplied to a limited invocation to the original function without changing concurrency enforcement or result propagation.
Expose live activeCount and pendingCount properties on the limited function, updating them consistently as work is queued, started, settled, and drained.
Support functions that return synchronously and functions that throw synchronously, settling the returned promise with the value or error while releasing capacity for queued work.
For pMapIterable, pass each input's zero-based source index to the mapper and preserve that index across asynchronous scheduling.
Allow pMapIterable to consume iterator entries that are promises, awaiting each entry before invoking the mapper while preserving concurrency and backpressure bounds.
Add a drain method that returns an iterator over all values in queue order, dequeues each yielded value, includes undefined values, and finishes with an empty queue, with matching types.
At runtime, callCount must reject a function that was not wrapped by onetime and continue reporting counts for valid wrapped functions.
Support delays beyond the platform timer maximum by scheduling bounded timer segments until the requested duration elapses, without resolving immediately on overflow.
Include the range helper in createWithTimers return values and preserve the timer-injection behavior and other returned helpers.
When timers are not explicitly injected, resolve setTimeout and clearTimeout when a delay is created so fake timers installed after module import are honored.
Run limited work in the caller's asynchronous resource context so AsyncLocalStorage or equivalent async-hook state propagates across queued execution.
Never invoke a limited function in the submitting call stack; schedule it asynchronously even when capacity is immediately available, while preserving ordering and rejection behavior.
Expose a validated mutable concurrency property whose increases and decreases affect subsequent scheduling without exceeding the new limit or losing queued work, with matching types.
If the supplied signal is already aborted, reject without leaving an abort listener attached; preserve normal abort behavior for a live signal.
For pMapIterable promise inputs that settle out of order, pass the mapper each element's original source index rather than its settlement order.
For pMapIterable over asynchronous input, never run more mappers than the configured concurrency even when backpressure is larger, while continuing to make progress.
Remove the exact abort listener after pMap settles successfully, fails, or aborts so repeated operations do not retain listeners.
Accept an AbortSignal option, reject promptly with the signal's abort reason when aborted, stop starting avoidable new work, and declare the option in TypeScript and documentation.
Convert synchronous iterator failures and mapper promise failures into the returned operation's rejection without producing unhandled promise rejections, while settling already-started work safely.
With stopOnError enabled, stop requesting or starting new mapper work after the first failure while rejecting with that failure and safely observing already-started work.
When dequeue removes the final item, clear both head and tail references so the removed value is collectible and subsequent enqueue/dequeue behavior remains correct.
Run cleanup exactly once for each delay settlement path, including resolve, reject, and abort, without changing the externally observed settlement value or reason.
